primitives.note: Q, W, E deal on-cast/near-instant magic damage on cooldown; R's initial missile hit is also a plain cast.
Shadow Surge has two separately-timed damage instances: the initial missile hit, then a free recast dash-strike that deals larger damage and consumes the mark.
Personal Space's shield component only matters in the survival fight, not the damage fight.
All four abilities cost mana (W flat 75, others scale by rank); over a 15s window with limited mana regen this can cap how often Q/W/E are recast.
R's cooldown is stated to start post-effect of the initial cast rather than on button press, changing when it is available again relative to a naive on-cast cooldown model.

needsBespoke.why: Vex's kit reduces to standard plain casts plus one recast-or-multipart ultimate; nothing requires bespoke logic beyond the listed primitives. The Passive (Doom 'n Gloom) is deliberately excluded from primitives: Gloom only marks enemies that dash or blink, which a stationary target dummy never does, so under the stated fight rules the passive's bonus damage and Doom's CDR refund cannot trigger and Doom's own empowerment only grants knockdown/fear (crowd control, explicitly ignored).

unsettled.question: Should the damage fight simulator model any passive (P) damage at all, given Gloom requires the target to dash/blink and the target dummy is stationary and never dashes?
options: P contributes zero damage in the damage fight; Doom's periodic empowerment only ever grants CC (ignored) since Gloom can never be applied to a non-moving dummy

The simulator should assume some artificial periodic Gloom application (e.g. treat Doom's ready state as always able to detonate) to approximate real play, adding VexP#GloomProcCalc damage on some cadence
quotes: Nearby enemy {{tip|champions}} and {{tip|monsters}} that {{tip|dash}} or {{tip|blink}} will be marked with ''Gloom''

unsettled.question: Does Vex's basic attack (used to weave between spell casts) ever detonate a Gloom mark or otherwise interact with Doom in the damage fight, or is it a plain, unmodified basic attack given the dummy never dashes?
options: Plain basic attacks only; no Gloom/Doom interaction is reachable against a stationary dummy
Some other passive trigger (untested/undocumented) still allows Doom to fire off cooldown against any target, adding periodic bonus damage to an attack or ability
quotes: '''Vex's''' next {{tip|basic attack}}, which becomes {{tip|projectile|non-projectile}}, or basic ability hit against an enemy with ''Gloom'' will detonate the mark

proposal: Open the fight with Shadow Surge (R) fired directly at the dummy to land the initial missile hit and apply the mark.
Immediately recast Shadow Surge to dash in and land the larger recast damage instance (this is Vex's single largest burst and her only long-cooldown resource, so front-load it).
Weave in Mistral Bolt (Q) on cooldown throughout the fight, since it has the shortest cooldown (8s down to 4s) and highest AP ratio among the basic abilities.
Cast Looming Darkness (E) on cooldown for its magic damage, prioritizing it whenever mana allows since its cooldown is fixed and independent of rank.
Cast Personal Space (W) on cooldown for its magic damage component even though its shield is irrelevant in the pure damage fight; its damage still contributes to total output.
Fill all remaining time between ability cooldowns with basic attacks against the dummy.
Do not expect or rely on any Gloom/Doom passive proc, since the stationary dummy never dashes or blinks to apply the Gloom mark.
Do not plan for a second full use of R within the 15s window; its cooldown (140s down to 100s) is far longer than the fight duration, so only the opening cast-and-recast sequence is available.
questions: Given mana costs scale up by rank on Q/W/E/R (and Vex's base mana/regen at the assumed level), is there enough mana to cast every ability on cooldown for the full 15s, or does the simulator need to model a point where casts are skipped for lack of mana?

Should R be cast immediately at t=0, or is there a benefit to holding it briefly so its recast damage lands after some Q/W/E damage has already reduced the dummy's health (relevant only if execute-style interactions existed, which they don't here, but worth confirming there's no hidden order dependency)?

Is the dummy ever treated as 'moving' or capable of triggering Gloom via any built-in dash-like behavior in the simulator's target-dummy implementation, which would change whether P's Gloom/Doom mechanic should be modeled at all?

Does basic-attack weave order matter (i.e., should attacks be delayed to line up with ability cooldowns, or fired continuously regardless of upcoming casts) for maximizing total damage in the 15s window?
